# Purpose

`curveSS()` turns a Stock Synthesis report into the series needed for an
equilibrium production plot: the historical trajectory, the equilibrium yield
curve, MSY reference points, and the right-triangle used to scale the panel.

The input is either one `r4ss::SS_output()` list, or a named list of run
directories. A list of paths is read one run at a time and bound with an `id`
column.

# What comes back

`curveSS()` returns a list:

- `tseries` — year, total biomass, SSB, yield, surplus production and the
  equilibrium yield at that SSB
- `curve` — equilibrium yield against SSB
- `refpts` — MSY yield and the SSB at which it occurs
- `triangle` — the four corners used as the plot's upper bound
- `derived` — the SS3 derived quantities named in the reference-point set
  (`SSB_MSY`, `Dead_Catch_MSY`, `B_MSY/SSB_unfished`, and the unfished levels)

Surplus production on the trajectory is the accounting identity

$$
SP_y = B_{y+1} - B_y + Y_y
$$

using total biomass, not SSB. The equilibrium curve is a spline through
`equil_yield`.

# One run

```{r one-run, eval=FALSE}
library(r4ss)
library(FLRebuild)

ss <- SS_output("path/to/run")
parts <- curveSS(ss)

parts$refpts
head(parts$tseries)
```

# Several runs

Names become the `id` column. Use them to overlay scenarios.

```{r several-runs, eval=FALSE}
runs <- list(
  base = "path/to/base",
  highM = "path/to/highM"
)
parts <- curveSS(runs)
unique(parts$tseries$id)
```

`maxY` (default 1.5) only stretches the triangle above the largest of the
historical and equilibrium yields. It does not change the curve or the
reference points.
